response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.state_county_province AS st, COUNT(a.account_id) AS cnt FROM Customers cu LEFT JOIN Accounts a ON a.customer_id = cu.customer_id GROUP BY cu.state_county_province), s AS (SELECT st, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT st, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM t WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: The set of states comes from Customers, so a state whose customers hold no accounts counts as a state with count 0 and share 0. It is included in the average across states. NULL states form one group, via GROUP BY.
Shares are computed as unrounded decimals (count * 1.0 / total) to avoid integer division.

alternatives.interpretation: Only states that actually have at least one account are treated as states, so zero-account states are excluded from the average.
